title: Right to left language support
when: The site must support Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu, or mixed direction text displays in the wrong order.
inputs: which pages or languages are right to left
prompt:
Goal: Layouts that mirror correctly with dir="rtl", using logical CSS properties, with mixed direction text kept readable.
Steps:
1. Set <html lang="ar" dir="rtl"> for right to left locales and update both when the language changes.
2. Replace physical properties with logical ones: margin-inline-start, padding-inline-end, inset-inline-start, text-align: start, border-inline-start.
3. Flex and grid follow dir automatically; remove manual row-reverse hacks.
4. Mirror directional icons (arrows, back, progress) with :dir(rtl) or [dir="rtl"] and transform: scaleX(-1); do not mirror logos or media controls.
5. Wrap user content of unknown direction in <bdi> or set dir="auto" on inputs and text blocks.
6. Test with real right to left text, including numbers and Latin words inside sentences.
Quality bar:
- No left or right in layout CSS except for intentional cases.
- Reading order matches the visual order.
- Form fields align to the start edge.
Pitfalls:
- Mirroring with transform on the whole page.
- Hard coded float: left in components.
- Phone numbers and code reversed because of missing isolation.
Verify:
- [ ] html has lang and dir for rtl pages.
- [ ] Layout CSS uses logical properties.
- [ ] Directional icons mirror.
- [ ] CSS braces balance.
Output: Updated CSS with logical properties and HTML with dir handling.

examples.input: preciso do site em árabe também
examples.output: dir="rtl" on html for ar, margin-inline and inset-inline everywhere, arrow icons mirrored with :dir(rtl)
